caption: The drawing depicts a scene with numerous human figures, most of whom are wearing red, blue, or white garments and helmets of various designs, some adorned with feathers. The central focus is a large wooden cross being carried and supported by several figures. One figure in the center, dressed in red and partially beneath the cross, is falling forward with arms outstretched; this figure is surrounded by others who are pushing, pulling ropes, or holding the cross. Several of the figures wear tunics and hats with vertical plumes, while one figure on the right side, dressed in white and red with a feathered helmet, sits mounted on a light brown horse. Behind the horse, there is a gray stone structure with arches. Numerous spears or lances are visible, held by figures mostly in the background. The color palette includes earth tones, with dominant reds, blues, tans, and browns, and the background is a muted brown shade. The upper left of the drawing contains text that reads "#3 Jesus Falls The First Time."
title: Station of the Cross No. 3: "Jesus Falls the First Time"
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
